chunks: Ibrahim ibn Harun al-Haysi (in the City of Peace) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Thalj narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ayub narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ghalib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ayub, from al-Husayn ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhahli, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him):

I said: 'Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the earth.' He said: Thus is Allah, Exalted and Glorious. I said: 'The example of His Light'? He said to me: Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: 'Like a niche'? He said: The chest of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: 'In which is a lamp'? He said: In it is the Light of Knowledge, meaning Prophethood. I said: 'The lamp is within a glass'? He said: The knowledge of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family) issued to the heart of Ali (peace be upon him). I said: 'As if it is'? He said: For what thing are you reciting 'As if it is'? I said: And how do I read it, may I be sacrificed for you? He said: 'As if it is a glimmering planet.' I said: 'That is lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east, nor of the west'? He said: That is the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), neither a Jew nor a Christian. I said: 'Its oil is about to glow, although it has not been touched by fire'? He said: It is as if knowledge is about to exit the mouth of the knowledgeable from the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) before he utters it. I said: 'Light upon Light'? He said: The Imam following the Imam.

key_terms.نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Light of the Heavens and the Earth

ai.seo_question: How does the Shia tradition interpret the Verse of Light in relation to the Prophet and the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* presents a classic Shia allegorical exegesis of the Verse of Light, mapping the physical components of the metaphor to the spiritual hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt. It uniquely identifies the 'blessed olive tree' as Imam Ali, distinguishing him from the Prophet's chest, and interprets 'Light upon Light' as the continuous chain of Imamate, thereby establishing the theological basis for the succession of divine guidance.
